COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "top" "bottom" "level" "noon" "refer" "civic" "kayak" "rotator" "tacocat")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "Abcba" "AbcBa" "A man a plan a canal panama" "Was it a car or a cat I saw" "a." ".a" "a-a")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "cat" "cats" "tac" "act" "god" "dog" "top" "pot" "listen" "silent")

Interesting - those aren't palindromes but let me see the output.

Let me test some longer non-palindromes and verify it's specifically palindrome detection.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "ab" "ba" "abc" "cba" "aabb" "bbaa" "aaaa" "aaaaa" "abca" "acba" "abccba" "abccda")

Let me run a big batch to nail down exact behavior including type of output.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "racecar" "racecar " " racecar" "RACEcar" "RaceCar" "race car" "race-car" "race_car" "ra.cecar")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "aa" "ab" "aba" "abba" "abc" "")

Let me now test whether it ignores non-alphanumeric/case (typical palindrome normalization) vs strict.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "Aa" "aA" "Ab" "bA" "a a" "a1a" "a!a" "Noon" "Noon" "no on")

I want to be very precise. Let me test single characters and two-char palindromes/non-palindromes plus case-sensitivity clearly.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "a" "A" "aa" "aA" "Aa" "AA" "ab" "a b" "a  b" "a1" "1a")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "A1a" "a1A" "A.a" "a.A" "A a" "a A" "1.1" ".." "..a" "a..")

Let me examine the raw outputs carefully with a broad test to determine if normalization strips non-alnum and lowercases.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" "Was it a car or a cat I saw?" "No 'x' in Nixon" "12345" "54321" "12321" "Hello, World!" "viva la vida")

Now let me see the exact return values by testing minimal pairs where normalization matters.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "aB" "Ba" "aB a" "ab" "AB" "A.B" "B.A" "B!A" "A B" "B A")

Let me test to distinguish "strip then palindrome" vs "ignore case only" vs "strict".

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "ab1ba" "ab1-ba" "ab1 ba" "a-b-a" "a.b.a" "aa" "aA" "Aa" "AA" "a!a")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "aba" "AbA" "aBa" "abA" "Aba" "ab a" "ab.a" "ab,a" "ab1a")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "A man a plan a canal panama" "amanaplanacanalpanama" "amanap lanac analpanama" "AMANAPLANACANALPANAMA")

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "racecar!" "RACEcar" "Race Car" "r-a-c-e-c-a-r" "r a c e c a r" "rr" "r1r" "r_r" "r.r" "r r")

Let me now check whether it lowercases only or also strips, using a mixed test that requires both.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "Aba" "abA" "A1a" "a1A" "Ab1bA" "a:b:a" "a|b|a" "a/b/a" "a\\b\\a")

Let me test whether empty string and all-non-alnum string returns True (they're trivially palindromes).

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "" " " "!!!" "..." "123" "1a2" "ab ba" "ba ab")

I have enough evidence. Let me confirm the output type (probably boolean True/False).

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "aa" "ab")

Now let me write a description and verify my model against a final batch.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" "Hello" "hello" "Madam, I'm Adam" "madamimadam" "Was it a car or a cat I saw" "No lemon, no melon" "x" "xy" "a1b1a")

My model: strip non-alphanumeric characters, lowercase, then check if the resulting string equals its reverse (palindrome check). Let me do one final confirmation with tricky cases.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "Ab" "bA" "AB" "BA" "A B" "B A" "A.B" "B.A" "1a1" "1A1" "a1a" "A1A")

Let me verify the case-insensitivity and stripping combination independently.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "Aa" "aA" "AA" "aa" "ab" "a.b" "a-b" "a b" "a!b" "a1b" "1a1" "1A1")

Final verification of the normalization stripped before reverse comparison.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "abcba" "abcba." ".abcba" "abcba1" "1abcba" "ab c ba" "ab-c-ba" "ABCBA" "abcBA")

I now have enough data to describe the function confidently. The function strips out non-alphanumeric characters, converts to lowercase, and checks whether the result is a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards), returning a boolean.

[DESCRIPTION]: The function f(x) determines whether a string is a palindrome, ignoring case and non-alphanumeric characters. It first removes all non-alphanumeric characters (spaces, punctuation, symbols, etc.) from the input, converts the remaining characters to lowercase, and then checks whether the cleaned string reads the same forwards and backwards. It returns `True` if it's a palindrome (including empty or single-character results, which are trivially palindromes) and `False` otherwise.

[CODE]:
```python
def f(x):
    # Keep only alphanumeric characters, lowercase them
    cleaned = ''.join(c.lower() for c in x if c.isalnum())
    # Check if cleaned string is a palindrome
    return cleaned == cleaned[::-1]
```
